title: Eigenvalues and q-adic absolute values
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $r\geq1$, $q=p^r$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$, with the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-tw-conventions]. Let $X_0$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $\mathbf F_q$, put $X=X_0\times_{\mathbf F_q}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and fix an integer $i$. Write $F=\Phi_X^*$ for the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-linear automorphism of $H^i(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ defined in [def-tw-frobenius-action]. A scalar $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ is an eigenvalue of $F$ if there is $v\neq0$ with $F(v)=\alpha v$.

Fix a field isomorphism $\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, with no continuity condition. For $\beta\in\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ define
$$
|\beta|_\iota:=|\iota(\beta)|,
$$
where the right-hand side is the complex absolute value of [def-weil-complex-absolute-value]. In particular, this convention gives $|q|_\iota=q$.

An eigenvalue $\alpha$ has $\iota$-weight $w\in\mathbf Z$ relative to $q$ if
$$
|\alpha|_\iota=q^{w/2},
$$
where $w/2$ is a real number and the power is the positive real power of [def-weil-real-power]. When $\iota$ is fixed, write $|\alpha|$ for $|\alpha|_\iota$ and say weight $w$ in this $\iota$-dependent sense.

split_report.summary: Q100 direct-delivery review: corrected the impossible ell-adic normalization (q is an ell-adic unit) to the complex absolute value through a fixed field isomorphism, as in Deligne Weil II (1.2.6). Made the eigenvector meaning explicit, retained the integer-weight clause, and cited existing complex-absolute-value and real-power definitions. Read all four dependency statements, checked the two source snapshots and related Lean definitions, and recorded actual Mathlib searches. This is a definition with no proof steps and no new nodes. The source error and counterexample are detailed in report.md.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the eigenvalue, absolute-value notation and weight clauses of blueprint def-tw-eigenvalue (master order 2591, current main order 2935), with the explicitly reported correction of its nonexistent ell-adic normalization. The enclosing sk-p-real-operations local-polynomial argument is unchanged. The complex-weight convention agrees with sk-d-real-weights and def-weil-frobenius-module-weights; neither states this global single-eigenvalue definition in full.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q100-97d712377 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 4 stmt_deps, both citers, the unit, the chapter, both blueprint snapshots and Weil II (0.2) and (1.2.1)-(1.2.6) in full. The source error is real. Both blueprint snapshots normalize by v_ℓ(q)=1, but ℓ≠p makes q an ℓ-adic unit: for p=q=2 and ℓ=3, v_3(2)=0 and |2|_3=1. The reciprocal of a non-archimedean norm also breaks the triangle inequality (1/|1+2|_3=3 > 1/|1|_3+1/|2|_3=2). The fix uses a fixed field isomorphism ι with |β|_ι=|ι(β)| and integer ι-weight |α|_ι=q^{w/2}. This is exactly Deligne's (0.2)/(1.2.6.1), and the chapter's sk-d-real-weights and def-weil-frobenius-module-weights use the same convention. The change is named in the report under Source error, as E7 requires. The node is not a target and does not weaken one. Checked: hypotheses match def-tw-conventions and def-tw-frobenius-action, eigenvalue is defined inline, the real-power domain holds since q>0 and w/2 is real, and |q|_ι=q. Small cases α=1, q, q^{-1}, roots of unity and H^i=0 behave correctly, and the weight is unique since q>1. No duplicate definition in the DAG (rg). Both citers (root-of-unity modulus, multiplicativity) still hold. No new nodes, no proof steps, no tool_uses, no SGA. For the maintainer: the report wrongly says the title was corrected. `title` is maintainer-owned and still says 'q-adic absolute values', so please retitle it. Please also record the definition change in HUMAN.md so the downstream semantic review is reopened. No fixes made.
